question: Explain when an entity must test an asset for impairment under Ind AS 36, how the impairment loss is measured and recognised, and when it may be reversed.
keywords: fair value less costs of disposal

points.label: When to test
points.description: At each reporting date the entity checks for any indication of impairment, from external sources (market value falls, adverse changes, higher interest rates) or internal sources (damage, obsolescence, poor performance); if there is one, recoverable amount is estimated.
points.basis: Ind AS 36, identifying an asset that may be impaired

points.label: Annual test regardless of indicators
points.description: Goodwill acquired in a business combination, intangible assets with an indefinite useful life and intangible assets not yet available for use are tested every year even without any indication.
points.basis: Ind AS 36, annual impairment test requirements

points.label: Recoverable amount
points.description: Recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use (present value of expected future cash flows from the asset); an asset is impaired when its carrying amount exceeds this.
keywords: fair value less costs of disposal

points.label: Recognising the loss
points.description: The loss is recognised in profit or loss, unless the asset is carried at a revalued amount, when it is first treated as a revaluation decrease; depreciation is then based on the new carrying amount.
points.basis: Ind AS 36, recognising and measuring an impairment loss

points.label: Cash-generating units
points.description: If recoverable amount cannot be found for a single asset, it is found for the smallest group of assets producing largely independent cash inflows; goodwill is allocated to such units and a loss is set first against goodwill and then pro rata against other assets.
points.basis: Ind AS 36, cash-generating units and goodwill

points.label: Reversal
points.description: A loss on an asset other than goodwill is reversed if the estimates used have changed, but only up to the carrying amount that would have existed had no loss been recognised; an impairment loss on goodwill is never reversed.
points.basis: Ind AS 36, reversing an impairment loss
